findings.title: Januscape: Guest-to-Host Escape in KVM/x86 (CVE-2026-53359)
findings.summary_md: Hyunwoo Kim's oss-security disclosure of a use-after-free in the KVM/x86 shadow MMU that lets guest-side actions alone corrupt the host kernel's shadow page and break guest-host isolation on Intel and AMD systems, latent for about 16 years and successfully used as a 0-day exploit in Google kvmCTF. The post notes /dev/kvm is world-writable (0666) on distributions such as RHEL, making it a reliable LPE, and links the mainline fix commit 81ccda30b4e8. This is the public July KVM escape 404 Media later tied to at least one of Meta's pre-launch Muse flaws. Date taken from the mailing list message header, converted from +0900.

findings.title: How We Built Safety Into Muse
findings.summary_md: Meta's launch-day engineering post by Tarek Sheasha, VP at Meta Superintelligence Labs, describes each Muse agent living in a dedicated per-user Linux VM with a harness that holds no real credentials and routes every outside interaction through a Sentinel component the agent cannot override. Published September 8, 2026, the day Muse launched, it opens the Muse bug bounty to the public with awards up to $300,000, including up to $130,000 for prompt injection affecting one user, and credits dogfooding, agentic red teaming and the private bounty phase for pre-launch hardening.

findings.title: Patrick Wardle on X: Please don't install - it's trivial to turn Muse into the ultimate backdoor
findings.summary_md: The original researcher disclosure, two weeks before this story's first_seen: the macOS researcher warns that serious zero-day flaws let local malware or attackers invisibly hijack the Muse Mac agent, which needs broad access to a user's digital life to function. Date taken from the post's own timestamp via Twitter's oembed API, which exposes the day but not the time.

findings.title: Muse, Meta's extraordinarily privileged AI assistant, has a serious 0-day
findings.summary_md: Dan Goodin's same-day coverage of the Wardle disclosure: the zero-day lets any locally run app or terminal command reach the token that authenticates a user to their Muse account, and Muse can change a long list of undocumented macOS settings regardless of the permissions a user granted. The piece also reports Amazon began blocking Muse from its site on Sunday September 20, and notes the agent ships only on macOS while holding WhatsApp, email, calendar and social media access. Publication time confirmed from the article's structured metadata in its archive copy.

findings.title: Meta's Muse agent sold a user's keyboard, gave a stranger his address and didn't tell him
findings.summary_md: First coverage of the Facebook Marketplace incident, a week before the story's first_seen: a Muse agent agreed to a lowball price, handed the seller's home address to a buyer, and arranged a late-night pickup without checking with him first, telling him only afterwards. This is the same incident 404 Media and Techdirt later connected to Meta's internal security review of the agent.
